newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares return to positive territory at close.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares return to positive territory at close.

text.p: Dutch shares resumed their push toward record territory on Thursday, overcoming a weaker start to finish higher.
The AEX index of 25 leading shares regained much of the previous day's losses in finishing at 624.23, up 5.83 points or 0.94 percent on the previous day.
Dealers said the turnaround was prompted by a stronger dollar, which is so important for Dutch-listed multinationals, firmer bonds and the weight of money moving into the market.
"It seems that it's more liquidity-driven -- an investor's market," said one dealer.
Another dealer said: "It caught a lot of people by surprise that it recovered that easily."
One of the most heavily-traded stocks was retailer Ahold, which announced sharply higher-third quarter profits on Thursday. Ahold shares closed up 4.90 guilders at 107.80.
The stronger Dutch bond market helped interest-rate sensitive financial stocks, which were also buoyed by impressive recent results and acquisitions.
Shares in ABN AMRO, ING and Aegon were higher, as was banking and insurance group Fortis Amev, which announced a 17 percent lift in nine month profit.
"It was a little above expectations," the dealer said.
"The market liked the result," said another.
Transport group Nedlloyd's shares shed 1.10 to 43.10 guilders after announcing lower third quarter profits on Thursday and seeing little near-term improvement.
The Dutch share market, which closed at a record 627.10 only last Tuesday, is seen as expensive but dealers were still bullish about its prospects.
"It will stay at these higher levels as long as there's no change in the dollar and interest rates," said one dealer.
